read_scope: Full changed unix_io.rs, exact insertion/inverse, original/final wrappers and preservation proof, changed-loop diagnostics, fixed Tokio send/is_closed/reserve/semaphore and AsyncFd registration bodies, author verifier and source/evidence qualification. All 69 frozen members independently hashed; original source-map and full-tree projected, and isolated author proof fully replayed. This is not a claim of independently executing Rust or rereading every unchanged product leaf.

findings.finding: The branch runs only after a successful nonzero read. Tokio Sender::is_closed reports permanent receiver close/drop; a new send cannot succeed then. Skipping to_vec and send avoids work while retaining the full read-to-EOF loop.
If close races after the false check, the original allocation/send and SendError handling still run unchanged. No optimistic success or new buffer loss is introduced.

The unchanged AsyncFd::async_io await still reaches readiness and poll_proceed, and successful reads record made_progress in fixed Tokio 1.53.3. Removing failed-send work does not remove the loop's only cooperative boundary. Per-iteration budget use may change; timing improvement under the original load is not quantified.

Open receiver allocation/send/backpressure, 8192-byte buffer, EOF/EIO/Interrupted handling, writer task, stdin EOF, FD ownership, cancellation and both backend callers retain original bytes. In tests the closed branch still records Discarded(count), without recording Sending for a send no longer attempted.

Both original Intel failures observed only portable backend before the unchanged two-second deadline; preserved_fds was not reached. Relaxed diagnostic samples are not atomic protocol state; read_calls are not successful chunks. Neither those observations nor this optimization prove the timeout cause.

disposition: Source acceptable for root-controlled reviewable publication and its existing automatic CI. B21 remains OPEN; full original Intel context, every produced attempt, 31-case roster and original deadlines remain required. A future pass alone is not a causal proof for either previous timeout.
